articles.title: Day 2 of GKCM Award: Performances by Sarod maestro Pt. Tejendra Majumdar, Odissi exponent Lipsa Satapathy captivate audience
articles.description: Bhubaneswar: The 32nd Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra (GKCM) Award Festival, organised by Srjan - Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Odissi Nrityabasa in collaboration with Sri Sri University (SSU), Cuttack, continued its magnificent cultural journey at Rabindra Mandap in the Odisha capital on its second evening. The inaugural evening of this five-day festival on Saturday witnessed a captivating performance by veteran Hindustani vocalist Vidushi Shubha Mudgal. The proceedings of the second evening began with the welcome address and the traditional lighting of the lamp by the esteemed dignitaries for the evening, Guru Ramhari Das, Renowned Odissi Vocalist and Scholar; Poly Pattnaik, Founder, Mother’s Public School, Bhubaneswar; Prof. (Dr.) Rabi Narayan Satapathy, Vice-Chancellor, Jagadguru Kripalu University, Cuttack; Parthasarathi “Baboo” Panigrahi, Eminent Classical and Light-Music Vocalistalong with Guru Ratikant Mohapatra, Director, Srjan, and Dean, Faculty of Arts, Communication and Indic Studies, SSU. The musical segment of the evening featured an illustrious bearer of the Senia Maihar Gharana, Pt. Tejendra Narayan Majumdar, who interweaves Dhrupad, Tantrakari, and Gayaki into his music. He began his recital with the serene evening melody, Raag Shuddha Kalyan, that typically performed during the first prahar , between 6 and 9 pm. This peaceful, devotional, and deeply contemplative Raga evoked a tranquil inner stillness as dusk fell across the Bhubaneswar skies. His second presentation was a composition in Raag Jaijaiwanti, invoking and celebrating the season of monsoon through its deep, flowing notes, along with emotional depth. Conferred with the Padma Shri and Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, the Sarod maestro engaged the audience with his meditative and architecturally precise performance, ably accompanied by the vibrant rhythmic support of Satyajit Talwalkar on the Tabla. The powerful yet meditative sound of his Sarod play was complemented in perfect synergy with the cadence of the Tabla’s rhythmic notes as Satyajit Talwalkar also captivated the audience with his flawless technical precision, dynamic energy, and profound musicality. The second half of the evening shifted to Odissi dance, showcasing the artistry, vitality, and elegance of acclaimed Odissi dancer Lipsa Satapathy. Her performance opened with Pancha Bhuta , a grand and evocative production that beautifully depicts the five cosmic elements —Earth (Prithvi), Water (Jal), Fire (Agni), Air (Vayu), and Sky (Akash)— through sinuous dance movements and yogic postures. Set to Raga Malika and Tala Malika, this item is a choreography of Guru Aruna Mohanty composed to music by Guru Ramahari Das and Sumanta Kumar Mohanty and set to the rhythm composition of Guru Dhaneswar Swain. She then proceeded to perform Debagandhari Pallavi, a pure dance piece with intricate footwork, rhythmic speed, and graceful body movements, choreographed by Guru Bichitrananda Swain and set to the music composition of Guru Ramhari Das and rhythm composition of Guru Dhaneswar Swain. The presentation concluded with Kahibaku Laja , an evocative Odia abhinaya authored by Kabisurjya Baladeba Ratha. This emotive piece subtly portrays Radha’s shy, tender nostalgia after Krishna fondly embraces her, enchanted by her heartfelt veena performance. Choreographed by Guru Aruna Mohanty to the soulful music composition of Suramani Ramesh Chandra Das and rhythm composition of Guru Gangadhar Pradhan. A recipient of the Senior National Scholarship, Singar Mani, and Kala Ratna Award, Satapathy brought refined performance vocabulary and depth to the stage of Rabindra Mandap. She was supported beautifully byan ensemble of musicians with Rupak Kumar Parida on vocals, Agnimitra Behera on the violin, Soumya Ranjan Joshi on the flute, Sitakant Jena on the Mardala, and Rohita Pradhan on the Manjira. The proceedings for the evening were conducted seamlessly by Dr. Mrutyunjaya Rath. The programme achieved technical brilliance through the expertise of the Chief Sound Engineer of the festival C. Anand Krishna, while Bharath Krishna managed sound engineering alongside graphic design. The creative light design and operation were executed with precision by Debiprasad Mishra and D. Dhilip Kumar. On the third evening, Odisha will witness its first experience of theatre virtuoso Dr. Piyal Bhattacharya’s Marganatya , a revitalisation of the Marga tradition of Natya from Bharata Muni’s Natyashastra . Chidakash Kalalay - Centre of Art and Divinity will present “Saugandhika Haranam,” a must-watch play choreographed by Dr. Piyal Bhattacharya, set to Sayak Mitra’s music composition. Designed under the vision and meticulous direction and administration of Guru Ratikant Mohapatra, with flawless programme executionevery year by Debiprasad Mishra. The 32nd GKCM Award Festival 2026 is supported by the Union Ministry of Culture and the Department of Odia Language Literature & Culture Department of the state government.

articles.title: Bangladesh: Measles outbreak claims three more lives, death toll rises to 994
articles.description: Dhaka, Sep 6 (IANS) As many as three children died due to measles-like symptoms in Bangladesh in the 24 hours until 8 am on Sunday, raising the total number of confirmed and suspected measles-related fatalities to 994 in 2026, local media reported. The latest deaths were classified as suspected measles fatalities, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS). With the latest fatalities, the total number of suspected measles fatalities in Bangladesh has risen to 894, while confirmed deaths from measles remain unchanged at 100, United News of Bangladesh (UNB) reported. During the 24-hour period, the DGHS recorded 1,043 new suspected measles cases in Bangladesh, raising the total number of suspected cases in the country to 164,148. During the same period, 55 new confirmed measles cases were reported in Bangladesh, taking the total number of laboratory-confirmed cases in the country to 19,696. As many as 144,168 patients with suspected measles have been admitted to hospitals in Bangladesh since March 15. Among them, 138,772 patients have recovered from measles, according to the DGHS, United News of Bangladesh (UNB) reported. On September 4, Bangladesh's Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain said that a measles vaccination campaign will be launched towards the end of the month. While speaking to reporters after inspecting Sylhet MAG Osmani Medical College Hospital, Husain said that vaccine supplies have been ensured, Bangladesh-based Dhaka Tribune reported. As Bangladesh continues to witness a sharp increase in measles cases, a leading international advocacy group recently described the 2026 outbreak as one of the country’s worst public health crises in recent history, highlighting the concern that the disease is preventable through vaccination. In its report titled ‘Preventable Tragedy: Bangladesh's 2026 Measles Outbreak’, Canada-based Global Centre for Democratic Governance (GCDG) said that although the measles outbreak appeared sudden to the public, it was not an unexpected event from an "epidemiological perspective". The report noted that the crisis resulted from a combination of disruptions to vaccine supply and health programs in 2024-2025 during the former interim government led by Muhammad Yunus, along with missed routine vaccinations, cancellations of scheduled supplementary immunisation programmes, administrative delays in vaccine procurement, and a failure to promptly identify at-risk populations. According to GCDG, Bangladesh had long procured World Health Organisation (WHO)-approved vaccines through the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF)'s international supply chain; however, the interim government replaced this system with an open tender procurement process. Citing UNICEF, the report said the agency repeatedly warned the interim government of a potential vaccine shortage through five to six formal letters and around 10 meetings held between 2024 and 2026. Referring to Expanded Programme on Immunisation (EPI) data reported by Bangladeshi daily Samakal, the GCDG noted that measles vaccination coverage fell to 56.2 per cent in 2025, the lowest level recorded between 2017 and 2025. It added that WHO later identified the nationwide stock-out of the measles-rubella (MR) vaccine in Bangladesh during 2024-2025 and the lack of regular vaccination as the main contributors to the decline in immunity among children and the 2026 outbreak.

articles.title: MRVC ₹18.32 Crore Tender for Badlapur-Karjat Railway Power Infrastructure Works
articles.description: Electrical and Railway Engineering Companies Get Fresh MUTP-III B Opportunity Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation Limited has opened an approximately ₹18.32 crore electrical infrastructure tender linked to the development of additional railway lines between Badlapur and Karjat. The project forms part of railway infrastructure being developed under Mumbai Urban Transport Project III-B , or MUTP-III B. The tender, reference MRVC-W-404R , relates to modifications of traction substations and associated power infrastructure required for the third and fourth railway lines between Badlapur and Karjat. The official government procurement listing shows bidding scheduled to close on September 23, 2026 . Scope of the Railway Tender According to tender details, the project involves modification of: Two Traction Sub-Stations, or TSS , at VGI and KJT; One Sectioning Post, or SP , at BVS; and One Sub-Sectioning and Paralleling Post, or SSP , at Shelu. Associated work is also included to support the Badlapur-Karjat third and fourth line project on Central Railway. The tender value is listed at approximately ₹18,32,01,192 , with an EMD requirement of ₹36,64,100 . Important Tender Details Tendering Organisation: Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation Limited Project: Traction power system modifications for Badlapur-Karjat 3rd and 4th railway lines Programme: MUTP-III B Tender Reference: MRVC-W-404R Tender ID: 2026_MRVC_923285_1 Estimated Tender Value: ₹18.32 crore EMD: ₹36.64 lakh Tender Fee: Nil Bid Submission Deadline: September 23, 2026, 3:00 PM Scheduled Bid Opening: September 23, 2026, 3:30 PM Bid Validity: 120 days The procurement is classified under electrical works. Business Opportunity Across the Railway Supply Chain Although the main package requires specialised railway-electrification capability, its economic footprint could extend across a broader supplier ecosystem. Potential supply-chain requirements may include electrical equipment, cables, protection equipment, structural steel components, control systems, insulation products, testing services, fabrication, installation services, safety systems and specialised engineering manpower. For railway-certified or technically qualified MSMEs , contracts connected with suburban-capacity expansion can represent attractive long-duration market opportunities. Why Badlapur-Karjat Matters Rail capacity augmentation across Mumbai's expanding suburban belt is increasingly important as residential and economic activity pushes farther beyond traditional metropolitan boundaries. Railway infrastructure upgrades therefore have an economic impact beyond passenger transportation. Improved suburban connectivity can influence labour mobility, logistics access, housing development and commercial investment along the corridor. The traction-power modifications contained in this tender represent a critical enabling layer of that expansion. SMEStreet Perspective India's railway modernisation is not limited to locomotives, stations and new trains. Behind every capacity-expansion project sits a substantial B2B opportunity involving power systems, signalling, telecom, civil engineering, safety equipment, electronics, fabrication and maintenance. That creates an expanding opportunity landscape for MSMEs possessing railway-compliant manufacturing and engineering capabilities. Businesses interested in entering this ecosystem should closely monitor not just major railway EPC packages but also specialised electrical and subsystem tenders such as this MRVC procurement. Tender Advisory Prospective bidders and suppliers should verify qualification criteria, technical specifications, approved-make requirements and subsequent corrigenda directly through the official procurement documents before making commercial decisions.

articles.title: Government e-Marketplace (GeM) Signs MoU to Boost Recycled and Upcycled Textiles Procurement
articles.description: It is an interesting development by the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) to take an important step to foster sustainable public procurement with the signing of an MoU, which will boost the use of recycled and upcycled textile goods through procurement. This is an important development since public procurement has the potential to generate huge demand for sustainable goods. By promoting the use of recycled and upcycled textile goods in the purchase process through GeM, a big market for such items can be generated.
